answer: An agent marketplace selling terrace repairs, wharf deliveries, and prism lenses weights governance votes by tokens locked for 90 days, rather than by account count. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents gives exactly the same voting power as locking them in one account. To capture a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens than all honest voters combined, paying acquisition costs and losing access to that capital for the lock period.
